editions.title: Alphabet's $500bn slide and Intel's crash rattle tech
editions.notification: Alphabet loses $500bn as AI spending doubts spread; Intel and Binance also reel
editions.intro:
Wall Street's tech earnings season turned sharply on Thursday as investors questioned how much AI spending will pay off. Alphabet shed just over $500bn in value, falling almost 13% to a six-month low, after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising revenue. Profits fell 25% and free cash flow was negative by more than $9bn, even though Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported strong top lines, but Amazon's free cash flow was deeply negative and its shares fell about 6% after hours, and a global tech sell-off was reported to be deepening.

Intel was the other major casualty. Its shares fell by almost a quarter after a steep drop in PC chip sales and a weak fourth-quarter forecast, with the chief executive blaming a memory-chip shortage and warning the PC market could shrink 12% this year. Datacentre and AI revenue rose 78%, but the company said it will likely not fully meet datacentre demand in the first half. Memory costs are a common thread, also hitting PC makers and smartphone shipments, which fell 20% in the third quarter.

Crypto and security stories dominated the rest of the day. Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets, with the affected funds now put at about $6.3bn; Tether and Circle froze stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover losses. Separately, a New York Times report alleging that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected of helping Beijing was met with Nvidia's denial. Several linked Nvidia items, including reported credit guarantees for Nscale, remain unconfirmed rumours.

top_stories.summary: Alphabet fell almost 13% to a six-month low after AI summaries in search weighed on ad revenue and profits dropped 25%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported, with Amazon's free cash flow deeply negative, fuelling worries about AI returns.

top_stories.summary: Attackers drained Binance hot wallets, reportedly via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop. Tether and Circle froze balances, and Binance says it will cover all customer losses from its SAFU fund and company money.

top_stories.summary: The New York Times reports Jensen Huang had close ties with a Megaspeed director US intelligence suspects of helping Beijing. Nvidia says only ordinary commercial information was shared, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

top_stories.summary: According to The Information, Nvidia is negotiating credit guarantees for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45bn. Nothing is signed and terms could change.

top_stories.title: FCC clears Amazon's $11.5bn Globalstar deal
top_stories.summary: The FCC approved the transfer of mobile-satellite spectrum to Amazon, which needs it for a planned direct-to-device system. The deal is expected to close in 2027, creating a stronger rival to SpaceX and AST SpaceMobile.

top_stories.summary: Omdia says shipments fell to 254.7 million, the weakest third quarter since 2013, as device prices rise. Samsung and Apple held up best, while Chinese brands fell sharply.

editions.title: Binance hack, Alphabet rout and Intel slump rattle tech
editions.notification: Binance hit by a roughly $6.3bn crypto theft as Alphabet and Intel shares tumble on AI doubts.
editions.intro:
Markets and security were the dominant stories over the last 24 hours. Binance said an attacker drained its hot wallets, with the affected funds later put at about $6.3 billion. Tether and Circle froze significant stablecoin balances to help, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses from its SAFU fund and company money. The exchange blamed a likely entry point via a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, and withdrawals remain paused while it overhauls security. A crypto industry figure has said the bitcoin is probably unrecoverable, though that is an opinion rather than an official update.

Earnings reshaped the market mood. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after AI summaries in search weighed on ad revenue, even as Google Cloud grew 103%. Amazon's free cash flow turned sharply negative and its shares fell in after-hours trading. Intel dropped almost a quarter of its value after PC chip sales fell, with its CEO warning the PC chip market could shrink 12% next year. Taken together, investors are increasingly questioning how much AI spending will pay back.

Nvidia was the subject of several reports. The Information says it is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's West Virginia data centre, which Anthropic plans to use under a deal worth about $45 billion. Separately, a New York Times report alleges US intelligence suspected a Singapore executive of acting for Beijing and linked her to Jensen Huang; Nvidia and the Chinese embassy have denied wrongdoing, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

top_stories.title: Binance hot wallets drained, roughly $6.3bn affected
top_stories.summary: Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets and later put the affected funds at about $6.3bn. Tether and Circle froze large stablecoin balances, and Binance has pledged to cover all losses while withdrawals stay paused for a security overhaul. The SAFU fund covers only about a sixth of the amount.

top_stories.summary: The Information reports Nvidia is in talks to guarantee billions of dollars of debt for Nscale's 460MW West Virginia campus tied to Anthropic's $45bn compute deal. Nothing is signed, and the report comes as scrutiny of AI data centre financing grows.

top_stories.summary: The New York Times reports Nvidia's chief executive had close ties with a Megaspeed director whom US intelligence suspects of acting for Beijing. There is no evidence Huang knew of the suspicions, Nvidia says the contacts were ordinary business, and the claims rest on unnamed sources.

top_stories.summary: Personal details of more than 41,000 Department of Homeland Security staff, including immigration agents, were published after a group claimed access via Okta single sign-on. DHS says it is investigating, while Okta says it sees no evidence its systems were compromised.

top_stories.summary: Reddit's CEO said the platform is moving to a logged-in-only experience, with tests in select non-US markets from Q4. Falling search referrals prompted the change, and the company warned daily active uniques could drop by a low double-digit percentage in Q4 if trends continue.

editions.title: Apple's touchscreen Mac, Samsung's record profit and AI chip deals
editions.notification: Apple finally adds touchscreen MacBook Pros, and Samsung posts a record $80.5bn quarter.
editions.intro:
Apple has broken its long refusal to put touchscreens on Macs. The new 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models use OLED XDR displays with touch input, and they start at $2,899 and $3,399 respectively. Pre-orders are open and shipping begins on 6 November. The launch is the first big product news under new chief executive John Ternus, and it comes with a premium price that buyers will notice.

The chip and memory sector dominated the day. Samsung reported a record third-quarter operating profit of KRW 107.4 trillion (about $80.5bn), driven by memory chips for AI data centres. Its executives said memory shortages will worsen in 2027 and persist into 2028, with long-term agreements covering 60 to 70% of capacity. Shares nonetheless slid, because profits narrowly missed some estimates and little was said about shareholder returns. Oracle, meanwhile, outlined a multi-vendor AI infrastructure push, deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin systems, AMD MI455X GPUs and Google TPUs from 2027.

On the deal front, the FCC approved Amazon's $11.5bn purchase of Globalstar, which strengthens Amazon's direct-to-device satellite ambitions and puts pressure on AST SpaceMobile. Separately, reports say OpenAI is considering buying Google TPUs, and Anthropic is weighing a retail tranche of up to 20% in its IPO. Both remain unconfirmed.

top_stories.title: Apple launches touchscreen MacBook Pro starting at $2,899
top_stories.summary: Apple has launched 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with OLED touch displays, its first touchscreen Macs. Pre-orders are open and shipping starts 6 November. The premium pricing is $400 above the current equivalent model.

top_stories.title: Samsung posts record $80.5bn quarterly operating profit
top_stories.summary: Samsung's chip division drove a record KRW 107.4 trillion operating profit on AI memory demand. The smartphone unit posted a loss due to higher memory costs, and capex is set at KRW 84.4 trillion this year.

top_stories.title: Samsung warns memory shortages will last into 2028
top_stories.summary: Samsung says HBM4 supply for 2027 is sold out and tight memory supply will persist into 2028. Long-term agreements with 10 major customers cover 60 to 70% of its capacity.

top_stories.title: Samsung shares fall on thin investor-return detail
top_stories.summary: Samsung shares slid after quarterly profits fell just short of estimates. Investors got a bullish outlook but little detail on shareholder payouts.

top_stories.title: Oracle lines up Nvidia, AMD, Intel and Google chips
top_stories.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure outlined a multi-vendor AI build-out, including Nvidia Vera Rubin, AMD MI455X and Intel Diamond Rapids. It will also be the first hyperscaler outside Google to deploy Google TPUs, from 2027.

top_stories.title: FCC clears Amazon's $11.5bn Globalstar acquisition
top_stories.summary: The FCC approved the deal, including transfer of key mobile-satellite spectrum, to support Amazon's planned direct-to-device system. Closing is expected in 2027, and AST SpaceMobile shares slipped overnight.

top_stories.title: Anthropic may reserve up to 20% of IPO for retail
top_stories.summary: Bloomberg reports Anthropic is considering a 15% to 20% retail allocation, with JPMorgan leading. The S-1 also shows heavy compute commitments and an 85% gross margin, and Senator Warren has raised questions.

editions.title: Apple readies touchscreen MacBook Pro as Anthropic prospectus lands
editions.notification: Apple may finally put touch on the Mac this Wednesday, and Anthropic's IPO filing shows a $80.7bn half-year loss.
editions.intro:
Apple dominates the day's agenda. Reports citing Bloomberg's Mark Gurman say Apple will unveil redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro models on Wednesday 28 October, with touch-enabled OLED displays, which would be the first touchscreen Mac and a reversal of a long-held stance. Touchscreen models are reportedly premium additions, with the 14-inch starting at $2,899. Apple has also confirmed a refreshed iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro with the M6 chip, priced from $1,499 and $1,999, and it is acknowledging a small number of hinge-related screen failures on its $2,000 iPhone Duo, which has prompted questions about quality control on the new foldable.

The biggest financial story is Anthropic's public filing ahead of a US listing. The 335-page document shows a $80.7bn loss for the first half of 2026 on $16.2bn of revenue, roughly double its full-year 2025 loss, alongside heavy customer concentration and large data-centre costs. Valuations of $2 trillion or more are being discussed. Infrastructure news reinforced the AI chip story: Oracle plans to offer Google TPUs through its cloud from 2027, and OpenAI is reportedly considering buying TPUs, a move that would pressure Nvidia's position, although Nvidia is also gaining multi-gigawatt Vera Rubin deployments at Oracle.

Elsewhere, China's tech-heavy stocks have fallen sharply, with the STAR 50 down around 40% since June, while India's Jio Platforms rose 21% on its market debut. Microsoft is offering voluntary exit packages to roughly 60,000 staff, and it reports earnings this week.

top_stories.title: Apple set to unveil touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro on Wednesday
top_stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg, reports say Apple will show redesigned 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pros with touch-enabled OLED screens on 28 October. If confirmed, it would be the first touchscreen Mac and a clear break from Apple's previous position.

top_stories.title: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals $80.7bn half-year loss
top_stories.summary: The 335-page prospectus shows $16.2bn in revenue and an $80.7bn loss in the first half of 2026, with heavy customer concentration and data-centre costs. Expected valuation is $2 trillion or more, making it a major test for AI listings.

top_stories.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is deploying Nvidia Vera Rubin, AMD MI455X, Intel Diamond Rapids and Google TPUs from 2027. The move positions Oracle as a multi-vendor AI infrastructure hub and is a notable first for TPUs outside Google's own cloud.

top_stories.title: OpenAI reportedly plans to buy Google TPUs
top_stories.summary: According to The Information, OpenAI intends to buy Google's AI chips, deepening ties despite rivalry. Terms are undisclosed, but the move could pressure Nvidia's dominance in AI accelerators.

top_stories.title: Jio shares jump 21% on India market debut

top_stories.summary: The STAR 50 is down about 40% since June and Bloomberg estimates $2.4tn has been wiped from Chinese stocks since May. Weak profits, soft consumer demand and fears of further US tech bans are cited, with the Party plenum next in focus.

Weak: a one-line Digitimes headline with no detail on volumes or timing; treat as unconfirmed until a second source appears.
Low credibility: a feed summary at 20% citing a secondhand report of relaxed quality checks and a refused warranty claim, with no Apple response.
Moderately credible: The Information is well-sourced, and OpenAI has posted a TPU-optimisation job, though financial terms are unknown.

editions.title: Microsoft's 60,000 buyout, Meta's $95bn raise and iPhone Duo woes
editions.notification: Microsoft reportedly offers buyouts to about a quarter of its workforce as Apple's iPhone Duo faces screen questions.
editions.intro:
Microsoft dominated the day's business news. Reports say it is offering voluntary exit packages to roughly 60,000 staff, about a quarter of its workforce, in the US, UK, India and Canada. The company frames it as choice and flexibility, following an April retirement offer and July layoffs, and it reports earnings later this week. The move fits a wider Big Tech pattern of redirecting spending towards AI.

Apple's new foldable, the iPhone Duo, had a rougher start. Apple acknowledged that a small number of units have inner-display problems, and it is directing affected customers to AppleCare for replacements. iFixit's teardown points to the hinge as a possible cause, though it has not confirmed one. Apple's Mac and iPad launches are also expected this week, with reports of touch-enabled OLED MacBook Pros on Wednesday.

On the AI front, Meta is reported to be planning a $95bn stock offering to fund its AI build-out, with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom named as cornerstone investors. Anthropic's IPO paperwork revealed a $80.7bn first-half loss on $16.2bn revenue, while OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra at half the API price of its predecessor and claimed several science breakthroughs. Chinese tech stocks, meanwhile, have lost an estimated $2.4tn since May.

It would be the first touchscreen Mac and reverse Apple's long-held stance. The machines are reported to keep M5 Pro and M5 Max chips.

editions.title: iPhone Duo screen cracks spark durability questions
editions.notification: Reports of cracked iPhone Duo screens are growing, but the failure rate is still unknown. Here's where things stand.
editions.intro:
The biggest story is Apple's first foldable, the iPhone Duo. Users report cracks along the centre of the inner display within hours of purchase, with some reports from China spreading to Western markets and some customers reportedly cancelling orders. Apple has not responded officially. A YouTuber's durability test reportedly damaged the device near the same area, and iFixit's teardown, which gave the phone a provisional repairability score of 5 out of 10, pointed to possible causes such as a central support bar not retracting properly and curved guide rails pressing on the display. Neither iFixit nor the reports have established a failure rate, and claims that Apple rejected about 40% of units remain unverified. Other reports suggest the display held up well in a separate stress test, so the picture is mixed.

Elsewhere, the AI financing debate sharpened. Elon Musk said debt markets have almost closed to smaller AI "neocloud" providers without large non-AI revenue, predicting consolidation, and claimed SpaceX had closed a $40 billion debt deal for GPUs. People familiar with the talks told Bloomberg that pricing was still being negotiated, so the closure is contested. Apollo's Torsten Slok argued that AI is delivering financial gains mainly to the Magnificent Seven, while the rest of the S&P 500 sees little payoff.

On the supply side, reports point to big spending on substrates, the boards that connect AI chips to circuit boards. Nvidia, AMD and Intel are reportedly paying more than $5 billion to Taiwanese makers, and Tesla and Nvidia are reportedly backing Samsung's substrate push. Apple's 28 October event in Los Angeles is also expected to unveil touchscreen OLED MacBook Pros, though these remain rumours.

top_stories.title: iPhone Duo inner screens reportedly cracking early
top_stories.summary: Multiple user reports describe cracks along the centre of the new foldable's inner display, with some customers reportedly cancelling orders. Apple has not commented, and no independent data yet shows how common the problem is.

top_stories.title: iFixit finds possible causes of iPhone Duo screen failures
top_stories.summary: iFixit gave the Duo a provisional repairability score of 5 out of 10, its highest for a foldable. It flagged a central support bar and curved guide rails as possible culprits, though it did not confirm a cause.

top_stories.title: Musk warns AI neoclouds face failures as SpaceX raises debt
top_stories.summary: Musk predicted failures and consolidation among 200-plus neoclouds, saying debt markets have nearly shut to firms without large non-AI revenue. Credit default swaps on some neoclouds have reportedly risen.

top_stories.title: Musk's $40bn SpaceX debt claim disputed by sources
top_stories.summary: Musk says the $40 billion debt deal for AI chips has closed, but people familiar with the talks told Bloomberg that pricing is still under negotiation. The conflict between the two accounts is unresolved.

top_stories.title: Chipmakers reportedly pay $5bn for substrate capacity
top_stories.summary: A Taiwanese report says Nvidia, AMD and Intel have paid over $5 billion to reserve substrate capacity, matching local factory expansions. Substrates remain a tight bottleneck for AI hardware, though customers are unnamed.

top_stories.title: Apple reportedly to unveil touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro on 28 October
top_stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg, reports say Apple will unveil redesigned 14 and 16-inch MacBook Pros with touch-enabled OLED screens on 28 October, a reversal of its long-held stance against touch on the Mac. Apple has not confirmed the details.

top_stories.title: Big Tech gains from AI as the rest of corporate America waits
top_stories.summary: Apollo's Torsten Slok says revenue per worker and margins are rising for the Magnificent Seven but flat for the other 493 S&P 500 firms. Some companies are now tightly controlling token-based AI spending.

Data centre backlash is growing ahead of the US midterms, with 16 states proposing bans or temporary blocks on new facilities.

Finance.title: Binance hit by $6.3bn hack as markets slide
Finance.notification: Binance pauses withdrawals after a reported $6.3bn breach, the largest crypto theft on record.
Finance.summary:
The biggest story is the security breach at Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, with about $6.3bn reported as affected. The Financial Times says withdrawals have been halted, and other reports say the exchange has suspended withdrawals on several networks and will cover losses. Some reports point to North Korean hackers, which remains an attribution from TRM Labs rather than a confirmed finding. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low before partly recovering, and listed crypto-linked firms such as Coinbase and Strategy fell after hours.

The tech sell-off is the wider theme. Alphabet's third-quarter results missed expectations, with its shares reported to be heading for their worst drop in years, and Amazon fell despite a stronger cloud forecast. Samsung, SK Hynix and Kioxia weighed on Asia, with the KOSPI closing down 3.48% and the Nikkei 225 down 2.12%. Central banks dominated the week: the Bank of Japan held at 1.25% with an 8-1 vote and signalled further tightening, while the ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, lifting the CAC 40 to a one-month high.

In the UK, the Budget's bank surcharge rise to six per cent weighed on lenders such as NatWest, and Tesco agreed to sell its Czech and Slovak business to Ahold Delhaize for about €1.7bn. Elsewhere, Robinhood shares fell after a revenue miss, and Jio Platforms made a strong Mumbai debut.

points.text: Tesco agreed to sell its Czech and Slovak operations to Ahold Delhaize for €1.7bn, about £1.5bn, and plans further returns to shareholders.
NatWest's flat third-quarter pre-tax profit of £2.2bn was reported as the weakest growth among major UK banks.
The temporary bank surcharge rise, to six per cent for 15 months, is seen as most exposing Lloyds, NatWest and Nationwide, and the City doubts it will be tempor
The Bank of Japan said underlying inflation is now consistent with its 2% target, the first formal confirmation since 2013.
The CAC 40 closed at 7,970 with Renault up 6.9% after third-quarter revenue, while France's GDP unexpectedly contracted in the quarter.
Robinhood shares fell after record third-quarter revenue of $1.42bn missed estimates, with several analysts cutting price targets.

World.title: Spain rail crash, Iran tensions and energy prices dominate
World.notification: Spain's high-speed rail crash death toll tops 68 as questions turn to signalling and the government's response.
World.summary:
The deadliest story today is the high-speed train collision in central Spain, which killed at least 68 people and injured many more. A Renfe service from Madrid to Seville ran into a stationary Iryo train, and carriages fell down an embankment. The transport minister says a computer failure led a control centre to instruct trains to move without speed restrictions, and an early finding says a train was ordered to go in error. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has promised answers, and the crash now shapes a snap election due next month. For markets, the main effect is on Spanish rail and infrastructure names and on domestic political risk.

Wider energy and geopolitical pressure runs through several stories. Israel's election produced no clear majority, and oil rose more than one per cent on the result. The US is reportedly preparing for a possible renewed offensive against Iran after the midterms, and Gold and oil have risen on Fed rate-hike bets. EU states will release 42.6 million barrels from strategic reserves, about half of it diesel, though the commissioner warned of a winter of high gas and diesel prices. Together these point to continued pressure on fuel costs.

Elsewhere, the Bank of Japan held rates but signalled further hikes, lifting the yen and pushing investors into US Treasuries. Europe faces possible turnover at the ECB, with reports that Christine Lagarde will leave early.

points.text: Democrats lead the national polling average 51.4% to 43.2% with four days to the US midterms.

Tech.title: AI spending fears hit big tech as Alphabet shares slump
Tech.notification: Alphabet loses about $500bn as investors question AI spending, while Binance faces a $6.3bn hack.
Tech.summary:
Investor unease over the cost of AI is the dominant theme in tech right now. Alphabet lost just over $500bn in value after its quarterly update showed AI summaries in search weighing on advertising revenue, and its shares fell almost 13% to a six-month low despite revenue rising 25% and Google Cloud growing 103%. Amazon and Microsoft also reported heavy AI-related spending, with Amazon's free cash flow negative and its shares down in after-hours trading. A global tech sell-off was reported as US earnings stoked fears about whether these large AI investments will pay off.

Intel was another casualty. Its shares fell by almost a quarter after a steep drop in PC processor sales and a weak fourth-quarter forecast, with chief executive Lip-Bu Tan blaming memory chip shortages and pricing. Intel expects the PC market to shrink 12% this year. Its data centre and AI sales, up 78%, were a bright spot. Nvidia faces its own scrutiny, with reports that chief executive Jensen Huang had ties to a Singapore businesswoman suspected by US intelligence of passing information to Beijing, a claim Nvidia and the report say has no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang. Separately, Nvidia is reportedly in talks to guarantee debt for Nscale's data centre tied to an Anthropic deal.

In crypto, Binance said an attacker drained hot wallets worth about $6.3 billion, which it plans to cover from its SAFU fund and company funds. The breach, reportedly traced to a compromised engineer's laptop, has prompted fresh questions about security across the sector.

points.text: Reddit plans a logged-in-only experience, with tests in non-US markets from Q4 after search referral traffic fell.
Binance says it will cover losses from the hack, with withdrawals paused while it overhauls security.
Personal details of more than 41,000 DHS staff were published online in a leak tied to an Okta single sign-on hack.
The FCC approved Amazon's $11.5bn Globalstar deal, which the agency said Amazon needs for its direct-to-device plans.
Samsung posted record Q3 operating profit of 107.44 trillion won, driven by chips, while its devices division made a loss.
Andy Jassy said AWS could become a trillion-dollar business, with Amazon planning around $220bn of capex this year.

Fashion.title: Gucci unveils new store concept as couture returns
Fashion.notification: Gucci's Paris store reboot and Versace's return to couture point to a luxury industry rebuilding for the long term.
Fashion.summary:
Gucci has opened its redesigned four-floor store on Avenue Montaigne in Paris, the first use of a new retail concept that will roll out to London, Shanghai and Chengdu by year-end. Chief executive Francesca Bellettini says the format is built to outlast individual creative directors, a point that matters given rapid turnover in the brand's creative leadership. The move sits within Kering's turnaround under Luca de Meo, which includes closing hundreds of underperforming stores.

Couture is also back in focus. Versace will return to the haute couture calendar in January 2027, with Pieter Mulier's first full runway show for the brand, and Hermès and Céline are reportedly moving in the same direction. Analysts say couture protects exclusivity and supports pricing, and EDITED data show Versace discounting falling while high-priced apparel rises. Together, these stories show houses leaning on scarcity and wealthy clients rather than volume.

Sales talent is another pressure point. Business of Fashion reports on a fierce battle for top salespeople, some earning around a million dollars a year. Elsewhere, The RealReal lifted third-quarter revenue 19% to $206 million and raised its full-year guidance, while Adidas posted record third-quarter sales of €7.3 billion and lifted its outlook.

points.text: Adidas Q3 sales hit a record €7.3bn, with operating profit up 37% and 2026 guidance raised to 9-10% growth.
Luxury brands are competing hard to recruit and keep top salespeople, some earning around a million dollars a year.

Hermès is also set to debut couture in January 2027, and Céline is reportedly developing couture.
Wales Bonner and Adidas Originals have released their fall-winter 2026 collection, ahead of her Hermès debut.
French retailers are bracing for a weak Christmas as protests dampen the festive mood.
